guideline_statement: Normal fasting plasma glucose is defined as below 100 mg/dL. Fasting plasma glucose between 100 and 125 mg/dL indicates impaired fasting glucose (prediabetes). A fasting plasma glucose of 126 mg/dL or higher warrants clinical confirmation via repeat testing in the absence of unequivocal hyperglycemia symptoms.
clinical_context: Fasting is defined as no caloric intake for at least 8 hours. In asymptomatic individuals, screening results must be confirmed with a subsequent repeat laboratory test on a separate day before any diagnosis is established.

guideline_statement: During a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test, a 2-hour plasma glucose < 140 mg/dL is normal. Values from 140 to 199 mg/dL indicate impaired glucose tolerance (prediabetes). A 2-hour plasma glucose of 200 mg/dL or greater suggests diabetes and requires formal clinical confirmation.
clinical_context: The 2-hour OGTT directly measures postprandial glucose clearance kinetics. In the Pima Indian diabetes dataset, the 'Glucose' feature corresponds to 2-hour post-load plasma glucose concentration.

section: Criteria for Screening for Diabetes or Prediabetes in Asymptomatic Adults (Table 2.3)

reference_ranges.overweight_threshold: BMI >= 25 kg/m² (>= 23 kg/m² in Asian American individuals)

guideline_statement: Screening for prediabetes and diabetes using an assessment of risk factors should be performed in asymptomatic adults who are overweight or obese (BMI >= 25 kg/m²) and have one or more additional risk factors such as first-degree relative with diabetes, high-risk ethnicity, history of gestational diabetes, or hypertension.
clinical_context: Screening tools estimate probability of disease to prioritize clinical evaluation. An elevated screening score does not equal disease diagnosis.
